chunks: Al-Husayn from al-Fadala from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman from Sama'a from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person who fasts voluntarily and hunger strikes him: he said, 'He has the choice between himself and the afternoon prayer. And if he remains until the afternoon prayer, then it occurs to him to fast and he had not intended that, then he may fast that day if he wishes.'

key_terms.اَلصَّائِمِ اَلْمُتَطَوِّعِ: The voluntary faster (one fasting nafl, not obligatory)

ai.seo_question: Can a person break a voluntary fast due to hunger and still have it count, or must they fast until sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the reliable chain of Samaanah and Abu Basir, clarifies the flexibility in voluntary fasting by allowing the fast-breaker until the time of Asr. It further establishes that if one remains fasting past Asr without prior intention to continue, the fast is still valid, highlighting the leniency in nafl acts. This ruling underscores the distinction between obligatory and voluntary fasting, where the latter allows for more ease in intention and breaking.
